# Understanding Brief: subgroup shape tests

## One-Sentence Test Purpose

This test checks whether clustered subgroup partitions and four-invocation quad scopes have the required membership by reconstructing their member invocation IDs inside supported shader stages.

## Background Knowledge

### Subgroups, ballots, and invocation IDs

A subgroup is an implementation-selected set of shader invocations that can exchange data through subgroup operations. Each invocation has a `gl_SubgroupInvocationID`, and `subgroupBallot(true)` returns a bit mask of the active subgroup invocations.

Why it matters here:
- The test does not assume that a subgroup has one fixed size.
- Ballot bits let the shader distinguish active member IDs from inactive IDs when checking a shape.

### Clustered partitions and quad scopes

Clustered operations partition a subgroup into consecutive power-of-two groups. A quad scope contains four invocations. For subgroup quad operations, their subgroup invocation indices are consecutive and the first index is a multiple of four. These rules come from the Vulkan definitions of [clustered group operations](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/shaders.adoc#L3543-L3552) and [quad scope](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/shaders.adoc#L3283-L3336).

Why it matters here:
- A clustered reduction must not include invocations outside the selected cluster.
- An indexed quad broadcast must return the value from the requested member of the current quad.

## One Concrete Example

For `dEQP-VK.subgroups.shape.compute.quad`, the generated compute shader broadcasts `gl_SubgroupInvocationID` from quad indices 0 through 3. It computes the expected quad base as `gl_SubgroupInvocationID & ~0x3`, then compares every active returned value with `base + index`. The invocation writes `1` when every comparison succeeds.

The selected case is generated by [`initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsShapeTests.cpp#L208-L225). Its shape-specific body comes from [`getBodySource()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsShapeTests.cpp#L94-L151), while the common compute wrapper supplies the dispatch indexing and result write in [`initStdPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsTestsUtils.cpp#L1406-L1434).

## End-to-End Test Flow

```text
[host] select clustered or quad behavior, execution family, shader stage, and optional required subgroup size
[host] check subgroup operation, stage, and extension support
[host] generate GLSL from the shape body and the common stage wrapper
[host] create pipelines, a result storage buffer, descriptors, and work dimensions
[host] submit dispatch, draw, mesh, or ray tracing work
[device] derive cluster or quad membership and write one pass marker per tested invocation
[host] make shader writes visible, wait, invalidate mapped result memory, and scan every expected marker
[host] pass only if every tested invocation produced 1 for every runtime iteration
```

## Generated Test Artifacts and Bound Resources

### Generated or loaded program artifacts

- [`getExtHeader()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsShapeTests.cpp#L84-L92) enables ballot plus either clustered or quad subgroup GLSL extensions.
- [`getBodySource()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsShapeTests.cpp#L94-L151) emits the operation-specific membership check.
- [`initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsShapeTests.cpp#L208-L225) selects SPIR-V 1.3 for compute and graphics or SPIR-V 1.4 for ray tracing and mesh stages.
- The common subgroup utilities wrap the body for compute, graphics, mesh, task, and ray tracing stages. [`initFrameBufferPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsShapeTests.cpp#L168-L178) supplies the separate framebuffer path.
- Compute and mesh pipelines use specialization constants for local size. Required-subgroup-size cases rebuild and run across each supported power-of-two size in the reported range.

### Bound resources and memory objects

| Resource | Created/configured by host? | Bound to GPU? | Read/written by device? | Read back by host? | Why it matters |
|----------|-----------------------------|---------------|-------------------------|--------------------|----------------|
| Result storage buffer | yes | yes | written | yes | Holds one uint pass marker per tested invocation for compute, graphics, mesh, and ray tracing helper paths. |
| Framebuffer color attachment and copy buffer | yes | yes | attachment written, copy buffer receives transfer | yes | Carries the pass marker for vertex, tessellation, and geometry framebuffer cases that do not use an SSBO. |
| Subgroup ballot mask | no | no | shader-local value | no | Identifies active subgroup invocation IDs during shape checking. |
| Quad broadcast array or clustered contribution mask | no | no | shader-local value | no | Reconstructs the members that the subgroup operation treated as one shape. |

## What Is Checked

- Every checked output element must equal `1`; [`check()`](../../../modules/vulkan/subgroups/vktSubgroupsTestsUtils.cpp#L2640-L2652) rejects the first different value.
- Compute and mesh callbacks derive the number of expected elements from workgroup and local sizes before applying the same check.
- Clustered cases test every power-of-two cluster size from 1 through 128 that does not exceed `gl_SubgroupSize`. For each active expected member, the result of `subgroupClusteredOr` must contain exactly the same member bit as the ballot.
- Quad cases request indices 0 through 3 with `subgroupQuadBroadcast`. Each active expected member must return its own subgroup invocation ID at the matching array position.
- Required-subgroup-size cases repeat the runtime test for every supported power-of-two size between the implementation's minimum and maximum.

## Behavior Parameter Identification

> **Behavior parameter:** `opType` shape operation
>
> **Candidate values:** `clustered`, `quad`

The operation type is the primary behavioral axis because it changes the membership rule being tested. Stage family and required subgroup size change where or under which size the same rule runs.

## What Failure Means

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `clustered` | Incorrect consecutive power-of-two cluster membership, incorrect clustered OR aggregation, or incorrect active-invocation ballot bits. |
| `quad` | Incorrect four-invocation quad membership, incorrect indexed quad broadcast, or incorrect active-invocation ballot bits. |

A failure in either value can also come from stage-specific execution, result storage, synchronization, or host readback rather than the subgroup operation itself.

## Important Variations and Special Cases

- `graphics` runs the same body across supported graphics subgroup stages and stores results through stage-specific SSBO bindings or a fragment output.
- `framebuffer` isolates vertex, tessellation control, tessellation evaluation, and geometry stages using a color attachment and readback copy.
- `compute` and `mesh` vary local sizes, including dimensions smaller than, equal to, and not evenly shaped like the subgroup size.
- `_requiredsubgroupsize` compute, mesh, and task leaves request each supported power-of-two subgroup size. This extends the same shape check rather than changing the core rule.
- `ray_tracing` runs the body across supported ray tracing stages. Ray tracing and mesh are absent from Vulkan SC registration.
- Quad use outside fragment and compute stages depends on `quadOperationsInAllStages`; the support check rejects unsupported stage combinations.
- The mustpass file has 24 executable `subgroups.shape` leaves. No matching entry appears in `external/vulkancts/mustpass/main/src/test-issues.txt`.

## Questions / Risk Points for User Audit

- Is `opType` the right primary behavioral axis, with execution family and required subgroup size treated as coverage dimensions?
- Is the distinction between a shader-local ballot mask and a host-created result resource clear?
- Does the quad example make the expected four-member membership rule concrete enough?
- Is it clear that a common result-path failure can affect either operation value?
- No unresolved source, registration, shader reconstruction, or pass-condition risk remains after inspection.
